headline: High: Plane’s broad egress and file-upload surfaces create default data-leak and cascading-error risk when paired with langchain4j outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct prompt injection is not default. However, Plane can ingest file uploads and hyperlinks, and langchain4j can generate content that a user may copy into Plane. That makes manual bridging possible, but the blast radius is limited and not inherently automated.
conditions: IF a user copies langchain4j output into a Plane issue or note
IF Plane file uploads contain attacker-controlled instructions
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of untrusted model output into Plane fields
Require a human review step before creating Plane issues from AI text
Use a fixed template that strips instruction-like text
Tag uploaded files as untrusted and review them before ingestion

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plane touches files, notes, hyperlinks, and issues, and has broad network egress; langchain4j is open-source with no egress and no data classes touched. The pair can still leak sensitive content if Plane stores or forwards AI-generated artifacts, but the evidence does not show automatic exfiltration from langchain4j itself.
conditions: IF Plane stores sensitive issue text or uploaded files generated from langchain4j
IF Plane forwards those artifacts to external APIs or email integrations
mitigations: Restrict Plane projects to non-sensitive data
Turn off external integrations for the workspace
Redact secrets before uploading files
Use a separate tenant for AI-generated artifacts
Audit outbound integrations for file and note contents

C_capability_conflict.rationale: langchain4j has no filesystem write capability listed, while Plane explicitly cannot write the filesystem but supports multiple instances. There is no documented overlapping write surface, so direct capability conflict is limited to coordination mistakes rather than destructive contention.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external resource through an undocumented integration
IF an operator manually synchronizes their outputs into the same Plane record
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Avoid shared mutable backends
Assign one agent read-only access where possible
Document ownership of each Plane project field

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plane is an issue/task system that can operationalize outputs, so if langchain4j-generated text is treated as authoritative, errors can cascade into tickets, schedules, or notes. The pair lacks a built-in verification step in the profiles, so the pathway exists in default workflows even though direct automation is not proven.
conditions: IF Plane users create tasks or issues directly from langchain4j output
IF no human verification step checks factual claims before filing or scheduling
mitigations: Require source links for every AI-derived task
Add a mandatory review checkbox before issue creation
Separate draft and publish queues
Train operators to verify dates, owners, and commitments

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile, and both are open-source/self-hostable. The main compliance concern is operational: Plane can store files and notes, so if langchain4j outputs regulated data, the pair can be used in a noncompliant workflow, but that is not shown by default.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into Plane through langchain4j-generated content
IF the self-hosted Plane deployment is configured without required retention or access controls
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Plane
Set retention rules for issues and uploads
Restrict workspace access to approved staff
Review deployment settings against policy
